clue.text: Influence of decree on one parliamentarian

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it, so the decree follows the parliamentarian

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP stands for Member of Parliament
an act is a decree passed into law

explanation.surface: A question about how much a government decree sways a single member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an effect on something is to exert influence over it, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Procedure for rewriting a résumé

indicators.note: rewriting suggests the letters are written out again in a new order

parts.note: the accents are ignored, leaving the six letters of the word

explanation.surface: Advice on how to go about redoing your CV.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a step or course of action taken, a procedure.

clue.text: Woman welcomes round number to provide help with reception

indicators.note: welcomes means the woman's name takes the number in, containing it

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
ten is a round number

explanation.surface: A woman greets a figure to assist with a party's reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' suggests a party, but it is radio or TV signal reception.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial picks up radio and TV signals, so it helps with reception.

clue.text: He's left awful Jack, who's gone on an excursion?

indicators.note: left means these letters have departed from the notorious killer's full name

parts.note: Jack the Ripper was the infamous Victorian murderer
the pronoun with its 's, the letters h and e

explanation.surface: A man has walked out on a dreadful fellow named Jack, who has gone off on a jaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from Jack THE RIPPER: T RIPPER remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a person on a day trip or outing.

clue.text: Drink and smoke, turning into a layabout

parts.note: a slug is a swig or gulp of drink

indicators.note: turning tells us the word for smoke is turned round and read from its end

parts.note: a drag is a pull on a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks and smokes all day ends up an idle good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggard is a lazy, idle person, the same as a layabout or idler.

clue.text: Seafood, in a way, with special gusto devoured

indicators.note: devoured means the shuffled letters are swallowed inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: special hints at the letters being made into something different

explanation.surface: Seafood eaten in a particular manner with great relish.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster or crawfish, eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Spare longer-established fuel store

parts.note: gash is British slang for spare or surplus
older means longer-established

explanation.surface: A rather mysterious ad for a surplus storage tank of some age.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large tank holding town gas, a store of fuel.

clue.text: A mature person accepts a particle of flattery

indicators.note: accepts means the word for the grown-up takes the letter in

parts.note: an adult is a mature person
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A grown-up takes in a small amount of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive praise, fulsome flattery.

clue.text: Pardon Duke — his Grace is eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric says the letters are odd and out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A duke is let off, because the nobleman is a bit odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge someone is to release or acquit them, close to pardoning.

clue.text: Part of format that's rather dull

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that a certain layout or design is a bit boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matt finish has no shine, so it is lustreless or rather dull in appearance.

clue.text: Drunk, as tea may be

definitions.meaning: tea is served by pouring it into cups, a literal reading of the idiom

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone tipsy, while literally tea sits in drinking vessels.

clue.text: Change a little money to get vegetable

parts.note: to turn is to change or become different
a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I
p is the abbreviation for a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a few coins and comes away with something from the greengrocer.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root crop, a classic example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Man in omnibus composing funereal hymn

indicators.note: in places the man's name inside the word for the vehicle

parts.note: an omnibus is a bus, and a coach is a long-distance bus
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A passenger on a bus writes a mournful piece of music for a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' is a link word, not an anagram signal. A CORONACH is a Scottish or Irish lament sung at funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronach is a traditional Gaelic dirge or lament sung for the dead.

clue.text: Parliamentary candidates hope to communicate efficiently

definitions.meaning: voters mark an X beside the candidate they choose, so candidates hope to receive that mark
an idiom meaning to make one's point understood

explanation.definitionFit: Split one way it is receiving an X on a ballot; run together it means to put a message over clearly.

clue.text: Burden Managing Director with record, lifting the biggest prize

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to lade is to load or burden
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A boss loads his record and lifts top honours.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run LADE+MD+LOG is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: First place in Olympic competition earns a gold medal, the top award.

clue.text: A natural source of terror, perhaps

definitions.text: A natural source of terror, perhaps

indicators.note: source of picks the initial letter of the word after
perhaps signals the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A spider is a natural thing to fear.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairy spider is commonly a source of fear.

clue.text: Governor of stronghold imprisoned girl?

annotationWithheld.why: Governor of stronghold imprisoned girl? (9): wordplay is STELLA in CAN, where 'imprisoned' is both the prison CAN and the container indicator, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Kisses cause lots to get excited

indicators.note: to get excited suggests the letters become agitated and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Kissing causes a great deal of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word for to kiss.

clue.text: Horse that's not so sweet

definitions.meaning: a clothes horse is a frame on which washing is dried

explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a rack for airing laundry, and a less sweet wine is a more dry one.

clue.text: Cricket groundsman's house

definitions.meaning: the London cricket ground is named after Thomas Lord, who laid it out, so it is his ground
the upper chamber of the UK Parliament is the House of ...

explanation.definitionFit: LORD'S is the London home of cricket, named for its founder; the Lords is a chamber of Parliament.

clue.text: Permission to go ahead with removal

definitions.meaning: an official go-ahead, as given to an aircraft for take-off
the act of clearing something away, as in slum or stock clearing

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot gets official authorisation before take-off, and a sale clears goods away: two senses of one noun.

clue.text: Iago was this old.

definitions.meaning: Iago in Othello is an ensign, called this rank in the play

explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is an old word for an ensign, Iago's rank in Othello, and also means very aged.

clue.text: Former social worker, a recluse, providing accommodation for male

indicators.note: providing accommodation for means the recluse word houses the letter

parts.note: a loner is a recluse

explanation.surface: An old-time social worker, a solitary type, finds a room for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital social worker, the old title for that job.

clue.text: Ordinary goat's milk cheese, mostly acceptable

indicators.note: mostly means the cheese word loses its last letter

parts.note: chevre is French goat's cheese
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: An everyday goat's cheese is generally fine.
explanation.walkthrough: An ordinary is a simple heraldic charge, of which a chevron is one.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a chevron is one of the ordinaries, the simple geometric charges.

clue.text: Courteous chap born not on the right side of the tracks

indicators.text: not on the right side of
indicators.note: not on the right side means to the left, so the word for born comes before the railway

parts.note: a chap is a man
ne (from French) means born, used of a man's former name
rly is the abbreviation for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: A polite fellow who grew up on the wrong side of the tracks, the poorer part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on the right side of' reads as social snobbery but simply puts NE to the left of RLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannerly describes someone with good manners, polite or courteous.

clue.text: The epitome of coolness, one copper shed burden

indicators.note: shed means the copper's symbol is cast off and taken away

parts.note: the idiom 'as cool as a cucumber' makes that vegetable the model of coolness
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Some supremely calm person or policeman sheds a load.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one CU from CUCUMBER leaves CUMBER, an old word for a hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To cumber is to encumber or weigh down, so as a noun it is a hindrance or load.

clue.text: Delayed reaction from stand-in used 'before shooting of scene

indicators.note: before puts the stand-in word ahead of the filming word in the answer

parts.note: a double stands in for an actor in risky scenes
a take is one filming of a scene

explanation.surface: On a film set, a stunt double is used before a scene is shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a second, startled look after a moment's delay in grasping something.

clue.text: Inapplicable to railway? Not in some parts of the country

definitions.text: Not in some parts of the country

parts.note: N/A is short for not applicable

explanation.surface: A form question about the railway is marked not applicable in parts of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is a dialect form meaning not one or never, used regionally.

clue.text: Lack of surplus, thus not so much for queen to divide

indicators.note: the queen's name splits the comparative word in two, sitting inside it

parts.note: less means not so much
Anne was a Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A frugal household, with less to share out for the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanness means having no fat or excess, a lack of anything surplus.

clue.text: Dictator time after time holding 27 back

indicators.note: holding means the two time letters enclose the other piece
after joins the two time letters one following the other

parts.note: t again is the abbreviation for time
t again is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: back means the answer to clue 27 is read in reverse

parts.note: refers to the answer to 27 across

explanation.surface: An autocrat repeatedly holds the country back over and over again.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' points to another answer in this puzzle, a cross-reference; 'back' turns that answer round before 'holding' puts it between the two time letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, like a dictator.
